g.title: request_path
g.text: The path of one command, and who checks it
Dynamic view · one exec call from an AI client to its Pond · Crocodile 0.4.10
From the Crocodile's source and ARCHITECTURE. Frames are accounts: each is a boundary the kernel enforces.

g.title: client
g.text: Calls a tool on one Pond

g.title: legend
g.text: Sage box: the Pond family's parts
Grey box: yours or the system's
Frame: a Unix account, the outer
Blue line: HTTP; HTTPS to your
its file mode admits the caller
Grey line: systemd starts a process
Arrows point from caller to callee.
1 the client sends the call with its token
2 the proxy forwards it to the controller
3 the controller checks token, tool and
arguments; the token picks the Pond, and
only its group may open its worker socket
4 the worker checks paths and limits again,
takes a slot, opens its task socket (0600)
5 systemd starts a runner as the Pond's
account, in its own unit and cgroup
6 the worker checks the runner's account
and cgroup, then sends the command
The runner exits, systemd ends what is left,
the worker waits for an empty cgroup and
A Pond is trusted like a person with an
account on the host: no command filter.
The account is the boundary: a real
account, not a sandbox. root and the
The controller can reach every worker:
Ponds do not isolate against it.
File tools stop at the worker (no 4-6).
